perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s available perspective:

- Harold is managing a project and feels frustrated/anxious because his team seems unmotivated, affecting progress.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a friend/advisor he turned to for help and met at a coffee shop.
- Harold told Arthur his team seemed completely unmotivated, progress was suffering, and he was at his wit’s end.
- He heard Arthur advise that motivation can be tricky, that he should understand what drives each team member individually, that people need to feel valued/understood personally, and that he should have one-on-one conversations.
- Harold agreed to try this, thanked Arthur, and felt more hopeful.

- Harold told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them and believed it would help them work better together.
- He heard Team Member 1 say that could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it.
- Harold said he would schedule time with each and wanted to make the project a success together.

- Later, Harold noticed the team still was not responding well to the new strategies and felt disappointed/worried.
- He told Arthur he had tried the suggestions but the team still wasn’t responding and he was worried about the project’s future.
- He heard Arthur suggest there might be deeper issues: underlying problems, personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold agreed and decided to set up another round of meetings.

- In those meetings, Harold said he had noticed performance issues and wanted to understand concerns.
- He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few team members affecting work. Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts.
- He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold said he understood and would see about redistributing tasks to ease pressure, saying their well-being was important.

- Harold felt optimistic/empowered and believed addressing individual concerns would improve team performance.
- He told the team he had heard their concerns and would create a more supportive/open environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and would help; Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good concerns were being addressed.
- Harold said he was glad and urged them to work together for project success, saying their input and well-being were crucial.

He does not have access to hidden events, other characters’ private thoughts, or information not observed, heard, told to him, or generated by his own thoughts/decisions.
